
---
title: "An Application of Clustering:  Food Insecurity and Health in Western North Carolina"
output:
  flexdashboard::flex_dashboard
---
    
```{r, warning=F, message=F, echo=F}
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(crosstalk)
library(DT)
library(flexdashboard)
library(factoextra)
```

```{r, echo=F}
data<-read.csv("mergeddata.csv")
data<-data[, -1]
data<-data%>%filter(CountyName=="Henderson"|CountyName=="McDowell"|CountyName=="Buncombe")
data<-na.omit(data)
data$Uninsured<-data$E_UNINSUR/data$E_TOTPOP*100
data$Unemployed<-data$E_UNEMP/data$E_TOTPOP*100
data$Minority<-data$E_MINRTY/data$E_TOTPOP*100
data<-data%>%select(CountyName, CensusTract, Diabetes=DIABETES, Cancer=CANCER, Obesity=OBESITY, HeartDisease=CHD, Unemployed,  Uninsured, Disabled=DISABILITY, Minority, MedianFamilyIncome=Median_Family_Income, TotPop=E_TOTPOP)
normalize<-function(vec){
  return((vec-min(vec))/(max(vec)-min(vec)))
}

data.norm<-data%>%mutate( Diabetes=normalize(Diabetes), Cancer=normalize(Cancer), Obesity=normalize(Obesity),  HeartDisease=normalize(HeartDisease), Uninsured=normalize(Uninsured), Unemployed=normalize(Unemployed),Disabled=normalize(Disabled), Minority=normalize(Minority), MedianFamilyIncome=normalize(MedianFamilyIncome))
set.seed(13010)
result<-kmeans(data.norm[, 3:11], centers=3)
data$Cluster<-result$cluster
data$Cluster<-as.factor(data$Cluster)

data.pca<-prcomp(data.norm[,3:11])

 
```

**Advisors:**  Holly Rosson and David Abernathy.  

**Student Researchers:**  Gracen Alleman, Neylan Visnius, and Mason Hollar

### **Introduction**

Clustering is a data analysis technique that divides a dataset into distinct
groups, with each group containing similar data points. We apply clustering to
CDC social vulnerability and health conditions data to identify and map
geographic regions in Western North Carolina that are most suitable for targeted
outreach efforts by **Bounty and Soul:** a local food bank which provides access
to fresh produce and wellness education for individuals in Buncombe,
Henderson, and McDowell counties. 

### **Data**

**CDC PLACES** data contains percent estimates of multiple health conditions
for all census tracts across the United States.  **Cancer, diabetes, obesity,
and heart disease** were chosen to be part of our clustering algorithm because
individuals with these diseases would likely benefit the most from dietary
interventions from Bounty and Soul.

Similarly, **CDC’s Social Vulnerability Index**  contains estimates of multiple
social vulnerability variables for all census tracts across the United States.
**Median family income and percent minority, unemployed, uninsured, and
disabled** were also included in our clustering algorithm.

### **Methods** 

* **R Studio** was used to clean, reorganize, and merge the datasets. </font>
* 3 clusters were using the **k-means clustering algorithm**
* **Principle component analysis**, as well as basic descriptive statistics provided a characterization of the clusters
* QGIS was used to map the clusters.

### ** References**

* CDC Social Vulnerability Index 2022, accessed December, 2024:
https://www.atsdr.cdc.gov/place-health/php/svi/svi-data-documentation-download.html

* CDC PLACES 2024 for North Carolina, accessed December, 2024:
https://www.cdc.gov/places/

* This research was supported by a **SEEDS grant** from the **South Big Data
Innovation Hub**.

### **Results ** { data-width=500}

**Cluster 1** consists of census tracts characterized by predominantly above-average income levels, as well as the lowest rates of heart disease and obesity.  

There are a few outliers in this cluster.  

**Cluster 2** has average median family income, has the highest cancer and heart disease rates, and lower social vulnerability variables. 

**Cluster 3** has the lowest income, highest social vulnerability variables, as well as the highest rates of diabetes and obesity.
The outlier in cluster 3 (Carrier Park area in Asheville) has a very low
value of PC1. This tract has an extremely low median family income.

```{r, echo=F}
Health<-data%>%gather(Health, HealthValue, 3:6, factor_key=TRUE)
Healthsd<-SharedData$new(Health)

SVI<-data%>%gather(SVI, SVIValue, 7:10, factor_key=TRUE)
SVIsd<-SharedData$new(SVI)


``` 


### **Health Conditions**

```{r} 
plot_ly(data=Healthsd, x=~Health, y=~HealthValue, color=~Cluster, type='box',  colors=c('#F8766D', '#00BA38', '#619CFF')) %>%
  layout(boxmode='group', title="Health Conditions by Cluster", yaxis=list(title="Percents in Census Tracts"), xaxis=list(title="Health Condition"))


```   
 
### **Social Vulnerability**

```{r}
plot_ly(data=SVIsd, x=~SVI, y=~SVIValue, color=~Cluster, type='box', colors=c('#F8766D', '#00BA38', '#619CFF'))%>%layout( boxmode='group', title="Social Vulnerability Variables by Cluster")
```


### **Median Family Income**
```{r, echo=F}
sd<-SharedData$new(data)
```


```{r}
g<-ggplot(data=sd, aes(x=Cluster, y=MedianFamilyIncome, fill=Cluster))+geom_violin()+labs(title="Median Family Income by Cluster", x="Cluster", y="Median Family Income") +geom_hline(yintercept = mean(data$MedianFamilyIncome)) 

ggplotly(g)

```
### **Principle Component Analysis**

```{r}
fviz_pca_biplot(data.pca, habillage=as.factor(data$Cluster),  col.var="black")+theme(
  panel.background = element_rect(fill = "Gray95",
                                colour = "Gray95",
                                size = 0.5, linetype = "solid"),
  panel.grid.major = element_line(size = 0.5, linetype = 'solid',
                                colour = "white"), 
  panel.grid.minor = element_line(size = 0.25, linetype = 'solid',
                                colour = "white")
  )

```
